290696127_97348376.text: Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-producing neurons (hereafter CRH neurons) in the PVN receive stress-responsive inputs, and in turn, regulate both the autonomic nervous system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis

290696127_2caba1f5.text: .Noradrenaline (NA) has long been recognized as a key neurotransmitter regulating CRH neuronal activity (Itoi et al., 1994) . NA is released from brainstem nuclei such as the locus coeruleus (LC) and the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), which project broadly to brain regions including the hypothalamus, the cerebral cortex, and the hippocampus 10,11 .
